messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 - multiple nodes in infer-eu-west2 pool entering NotReady (kubelet restart flapping). AlertID: INC-2791. Link: https://alerts.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2791 :rotating_light:

alice: i got paged, grabbing context. will triage the eu-west2 infer pool.

alice: quick snapshot: kubelet restarts + container restarts on nodes infer-eu-west2-b{3,4,6}. Observed ~10 restarts in 6m.

dmitri: saw the same. journalctl shows repeated kubelet segfault followed by containerd OOM kills. snippet:
```
Mar 15 12:07:22 node-infer-3 kubelet[1234]: E0323 12:07:22 kubelet.go:202] runtime status: container "llm-serving" OOMKilled
Mar 15 12:07:22 node-infer-3 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 9876 (llm-runtime) score 981 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 12:07:24 node-infer-3 kubelet[1234]: FATAL: heartbeat lost, restarting kubelet
```

alice: running `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-eu-west2` now. output:
```
node-infer-3   Ready?       3d   v1.27   10.0.3.45   NotReady (KubeletRestart)
node-infer-4   Ready?       3d   v1.27   10.0.3.46   NotReady (KubeletRestart)
node-infer-6   Ready?       2d   v1.27   10.0.3.48   NotReady (KubeletRestart)
```

ben: yesterday we pushed nvidia-driver 532.12 to that node pool as part of kernel compat testing. ops logs show `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` with repeated `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` and `GPU hung` around the same times.

carmen: ok mitigation idea: cordon+drain the flapping nodes, scale up the cpu-only fallback pool (infer-fallback-eu-west) to take traffic, and flip routing to prefer dedicated non-eu-west region while we clean nodes. i'll run the drain commands unless objections.

alice: go ahead Carmen. also I'll open a rollback of the node image to the previous driver. we need to be careful about in-flight requests — set max-surge to 0 for the drain window.

carmen: running:
```bash
kubectl cordon node-infer-3 && kubectl drain node-infer-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
kubectl cordon node-infer-4 && kubectl drain node-infer-4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
```

ops-bot: autoscaler: scaling group infer-fallback-eu-west desired=0 -> desired=6 (requested by carmen).

alice: routing change in progress: patching router to shift 60% traffic away from infer-eu-west2 to infer-dedicated-global. command: `rbacctl patch route infer-router --json '{"policy":"steer","weights":{"infer-eu-west2":0.4,"infer-dedicated-global":0.6}}'`

oncall-bot: @alice @carmen @ben noted as responders. paging infra team for driver rollback.

ben: started nodegroup image rollback job (NG-ROLLBACK-2791). will revert nodes to driver 525.78 which passed previous smoke tests. job logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:09:42Z rolling update started for ng-infer-eu-west2
2026-03-15T12:13:01Z node-infer-3 image revert complete, kubelet restarted, node rejoined Ready
```

alice: customer impact - preliminary: about 8% of production requests routed to eu-west saw increased latency or 503s over a 4-6 minute window. most of the errors were retries that succeeded after rerouting. I'm drafting a short status update for support & statuspage.

dmitri: additional logs from runtime show repeated allocation failures before OOM: `std::bad_alloc` followed by CUDA driver fault. snippet from llm-runtime log:
```
[llm-runtime] ERROR: allocation failed: requested 1400MB, available 128MB
[llm-runtime] FATAL: cudaSetDevice failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION
```

dean: temporary runtime config we can toggle: disable kv_cache and lower max_batch_size for problematic models to reduce memory pressure. i can push that to the runtime config override for eu-west pool. should reduce OOM frequency immediately.

alice: dean, go ahead and apply. Carmen, keep draining the rest. Ben, keep the rollback rolling and watch for kernel/nvidia module warnings.

carmen: draining node-infer-6 now. one pod failed to evict due to local PV, forced deletion used. note: this caused ~30s additional latency for that request.

ops-bot: rollback job NG-ROLLBACK-2791 progressing: 4/8 nodes completed. ETA ~7m.

alice: escalated to infra lead @ben for next steps on driver testing and preventing future image flips. also opening follow-up ticket INFRA-2791-ROOTCAUSE for postmortem.

oncall-bot: Update: incident INC-2791 status -> Mitigating. Investigating root cause.

aleve-sre: (actually name should be eve-sre) eve-sre: i'm on secondary, standing by for handoff in 10m. if anything still flapping after rollback ping me.

alice: Handoff to @eve-sre at 12:30 UTC. current state: nodes being rolled back, 5/8 nodes drained, routing shifted to reduce customer impact, runtime config lowered memory pressure. runbook: https://playbooks.redwood.ai/runbooks/kubelet-flap-inferpool.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next oncall is eve-sre. Reaction :white_check_mark:.

alice: wrapping for now — leaving monitoring alerts and the runbook link in thread. will add final incident note once all nodes stable.

ops-bot: rollback job complete. all updated nodes rejoined Ready.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-2791 -> Resolved (mitigated) at 12:45 UTC. Summary: node image rollback + runtime config changes mitigated OOMs and kubelet restarts. Customer impact: transient errors/latency spike for eu-west requests, no data loss. Postmortem ticket INFRA-2791-ROOTCAUSE created.

eve-sre: taking watch. if anything recurs my handle is eve-sre. I'll start a follow-up on-call rotation check tomorrow.

alice: thanks team — great coordination. :thumbsup:
